title: Fixed-boundary functor objects with all vertices fixed are Kan
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and degreewise pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $X$ be a quasicategory, let $A\subseteq B$ be a simplicial subset containing every vertex of $B$, and let $f:A\to X$ be a simplicial map. Define the strict fixed-boundary simplicial set
$$V_f(B,X)=\operatorname{Fun}(B,X)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,X)}\{f\}.$$
Here $\{f\}$ is the one-point simplicial set mapped to the vertex $f$ and all its degeneracies; equivalently its $n$-simplices are exactly the maps $h:B\times\Delta^n\to X$ satisfying $h|_{A\times\Delta^n}=f\circ\operatorname{pr}_A$, with simplicial operators by restriction. Then $V_f(B,X)$ is a Kan complex: every map $\Lambda_k^n\to V_f(B,X)$, for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq k\leq n$, extends to $\Delta^n$. The space $V_f(B,X)$ is allowed to be empty; no extension of $f$ to $B$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.1.11 (Kerodon Tag 01P1), statement; the retained item route proves this by inner-horn corner lifting and absolute outer-horn prism extension plus opposites.

proof.text: Fix a horn $a:\Lambda_k^n\to V_f(B,X)$, with $n\geq1$. By the degreewise definition of the internal functor object in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], this amounts to a map $u:B\times\Lambda_k^n\to X$ equal to $f\operatorname{pr}_A$ on $A\times\Lambda_k^n$. Explicitly, if $t\in(\Lambda_k^n)_m$, evaluate the map $a_m(t):B\times\Delta^m\to X$ at $(b,\mathrm{id}_{[m]})$ to define $u_m(b,t)$. Naturality of $a$ makes these formulas simplicial; conversely restrict $u$ along $\mathrm{id}_B\times t:B\times\Delta^m\to B\times\Lambda_k^n$. These two formulas are inverse. Define $h$ on $(A\times\Delta^n)\cup(B\times\Lambda_k^n)$ to be $f\operatorname{pr}_A$ on the first subset and $u$ on the second. They agree on their intersection, so this is a simplicial map degree by degree. An extension $H:B\times\Delta^n\to X$ of $h$ gives, by the same formulas, the desired simplex of $V_f(B,X)$ extending $a$. Thus it suffices to construct this exact extension of $h$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.1.11, explicit fixed-boundary horn adjunction; agent expansion of the internal functor definition.

proof.text: If $n=1$, the horn is one vertex, so $a$ specifies one vertex $v$ of $V_f(B,X)$. Its degenerate edge $s_0v$ restricts to $v$ at both ends and is the required filler, for either $k=0$ or $k=1$. Equivalently, the corresponding extension is the diagram $v:B\to X$ composed with $B\times\Delta^1\to B$, and it is constant at $f$ on $A\times\Delta^1$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.1.11, dimension-one horn check, written out.

proof.text: Let $n\geq2$ and $0<k<n$. The map $p:X\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration because $X$ is a quasicategory. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-inner-fibration-corner] with $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and this $p$. Its corner target identifies degreewise with $\operatorname{Fun}(A,X)$, since the internal functor objects into $\Delta^0$ are points. Hence restriction $r:\operatorname{Fun}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,X)$ is an inner fibration. The horn $a$, composed with $V_f(B,X)\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,X)$, lies over the constant simplex $f:\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,X)$. Lift this inner-horn square through $r$. The filler restricts exactly to $f$ in every simplicial degree, hence belongs to the strict fiber $V_f(B,X)$ and extends $a$.

source.place: Proposition 4.1.4.1, specialized to X to a point; fixed-boundary lifting square.

proof.text: Let $n\geq2$ and $k=0$, and use $h$ from Step 1. Every vertex $b$ of $B$ belongs to $A$. Thus $h$ on $\{b\}\times\Delta^n$ is the constant simplex at $f(b)$, and its edge $\{b\}\times[0,1]$ is the degenerate identity edge. Such an edge is an equivalence: its inverse is itself and its two inverse triangles are constant degenerate 2-simplices. The edge $[0,1]$ is contained in $\Lambda_0^n$ even when $n=2$, since its image omits vertex $n\neq0$. Apply [lem-cbc-invertible-prism-extension] with $Q=X$, the given $A\subseteq B$, and this $h$. Its hypotheses are now verified, and it supplies $H:B\times\Delta^n\to X$ extending all of $h$. By Step 1 this is the required fixed-boundary filler. No invertibility of edges of $B$ is required.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.8 at the terminal base: all prescribed vertex edges are identities.

proof.text: Let $n\geq2$ and $k=n$. Reverse simplex orders explicitly: for $\alpha:[r]\to[s]$ put $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(j)=s-\alpha(r-j)$. This is monotone, preserves composition and identities, and applying it twice is the identity. For a simplicial set $K$ define $K^{\mathrm{op}}_m=K_m$ with operators $K(\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}})$. This operation preserves products and unions degreewise. The identification $(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^n$ sends $\beta:[m]\to[n]$ to $\beta^{\mathrm{rev}}$; omitting vertex $i$ becomes omitting vertex $n-i$. It therefore sends $(\Lambda_n^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $\Lambda_0^n$ and sends every inner horn to an inner horn. Consequently $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory: reverse any inner-horn problem, fill it in $X$, and reverse the filler. Reversing $h$ gives a map on $(A^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n)\cup(B^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Lambda_0^n)$ to $X^{\mathrm{op}}$, with its $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ part equal to $f^{\mathrm{op}}\operatorname{pr}_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Every vertex of $B^{\mathrm{op}}$ belongs to $A^{\mathrm{op}}$, so its vertical edge $[0,1]$ is again a degenerate identity. Apply [lem-cbc-invertible-prism-extension] to this map. Reverse the resulting filler once more. Involutivity restores the original $h$, including its constant $A$ part, and yields the required $H:B\times\Delta^n\to X$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.8, final outer-horn case by the explicit order-reversal involution; agent argument.

proof.text: The preceding cases fill every horn in each dimension $n\geq1$, so $V_f(B,X)$ is a Kan complex by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. No vertex of $V_f(B,X)$ was chosen without a horn as input. If the strict fiber is empty, there are no such horn maps, since every positive-dimensional horn has a vertex, and the same conclusion is vacuous. Thus no extension of $f$ to $B$ or nonemptiness hypothesis has been introduced.

proof_origin.place: Acyclic direct horn proof of Proposition 4.6.1.11, using 01BT and absolute 01DP instead of the isofibration theorem whose DAG split depends on this item; final horns treated by explicit simplex reversal. Sources read online; archival copies WANTED in report.md.
